title: Write and revise in chat
summary: Use a conversation to turn rough notes into a message. Ask for a second draft in the same chat.

intro.what: Use a conversation to turn rough notes into a message. Ask for a second draft in the same chat.
intro.features: Mail queued at 09:00. One test arrived at 09:12. Other routes have not been tested.
intro.exchange: Use a fictional mail handoff to test this surface.
intro.m365: Apply the same check to an approved practice note.
intro.developer: Try the example with a small local project.

sections.title: Where it stops
paragraphs: A draft alone cannot tell you whether a mail repair worked. Supply a test result before asking for a verdict.

sections.title: Plan and availability
paragraphs: The free plan has a session allowance. The number of messages can vary with demand.

sections.title: Best first example
paragraphs: Mail queued at 09:00. One test arrived at 09:12. Other routes have not been tested.
Write two sentences for a handoff. Separate the one test that passed from the routes we still need to check.
Check your result. The update names the successful test and leaves other routes open.

sections.title: Where it stops
paragraphs: A file left on your desk is outside the project knowledge you supplied. Add the right version before asking about a change.
sources: How can I create and manage projects?

sections.title: Plan and availability
paragraphs: Free accounts can create up to five projects. Paid plans can use retrieval when the project knowledge grows large.

sections.title: Best first example
paragraphs: Practice handbook, revision B: only closed requests go in the weekly count. The sample has two closed and one open.
Add the handbook to a practice project. In a fresh project chat ask for the weekly count and the rule used.
Check your result. The answer gives two closed requests and points to revision B.

title: Build a small tool in Artifacts
summary: Keep an editable output beside a conversation. An interactive counter is a good first artifact because you can test it in seconds.

intro.what: Keep an editable output beside a conversation. An interactive counter is a good first artifact because you can test it in seconds.
intro.features: The tally starts at zero. Count adds one. Reset returns to zero.
intro.exchange: Test a pretend queue counter with zero messages.
intro.m365: Try two rows from a fictional request list.
intro.developer: Run the smallest working screen before adding another feature.
sources: What are artifacts and how do I use them?

sections.title: Where it stops
paragraphs: A working preview cannot prove that a published copy stores data or works offline. Test those promises separately.
sources: What are artifacts and how do I use them?

sections.title: Plan and availability
paragraphs: Artifacts are offered on free and paid plans. Persistent storage on web and desktop is a paid-plan feature.
sources: What are artifacts and how do I use them?

sections.title: Best first example
paragraphs: The tally starts at zero. Count adds one. Reset returns to zero.
Make an interactive tally artifact with Count and Reset. Show the score as a number.
Check your result. Two Count clicks show 2. Reset shows 0.
sources: What are artifacts and how do I use them?

intro.features: A practice counter page shows the right number but calls its reset button Clear All.
intro.exchange: Test a pretend queue counter with zero messages.
intro.m365: Try two rows from a fictional request list.

sections.title: Where it stops
paragraphs: A code change alone cannot prove that a report is correct. Compare actual output with a known small example.

sections.title: Plan and availability
paragraphs: Usage and model access depend on how you signed in and what your account includes. Check the session status before a long job.

sections.title: Best first example
paragraphs: A practice counter page shows the right number but calls its reset button Clear All.
In the practice folder, find the reset button. Rename its label to Reset. Show the changed lines and the result of one reset test.
Check your result. Only the label changes. A score of 2 still resets to 0.

title: Rehearse a handoff aloud
summary: Talk through a problem and hear the answer. Switch back to text to check details such as times or file names.

intro.what: Talk through a problem and hear the answer. Switch back to text to check details such as times or file names.
intro.features: The queue held fifteen items before lunch and five after lunch.
intro.exchange: Use a fictional mail handoff to test this surface.
intro.m365: Apply the same check to an approved practice note.
intro.developer: Try the example with a small local project.

sections.title: Where it stops
paragraphs: Speech can be misheard. A spoken summary cannot settle whether you said fifteen or fifty. Read back the saved text.

sections.title: Plan and availability
paragraphs: Voice sessions use the regular allowance for the account. Push-to-talk gives you control of the microphone in a noisy room.

sections.title: Best first example
paragraphs: The queue held fifteen items before lunch and five after lunch.
Read those counts aloud. Ask for a one-sentence handoff and a separate line with the two numbers.
Check your result. The written numbers are 15 and 5, in that order.

title: Read a file or inspect an image
summary: Attach a supported document or image and ask a question tied to one visible detail. Use a small file first.

intro.what: Attach a supported document or image and ask a question tied to one visible detail. Use a small file first.
intro.features: A short practice PDF has a table showing 2 requests open and 3 closed.
intro.exchange: Trace a delivery claim back to the sample report.
intro.m365: Find the exact line in a practice policy.
intro.developer: Keep the input files beside your test results.

sections.title: Where it stops
paragraphs: A blurry screenshot cannot establish what a missing digit says. Ask for unknown rather than filling it in.

sections.title: Plan and availability
paragraphs: Chat and project uploads have different limits. The upload guide lists 20 files per chat and a smaller per-file size for project knowledge.

sections.title: Best first example
paragraphs: A short practice PDF has a table showing 2 requests open and 3 closed.
Attach the practice page. Name both row labels, give their values and calculate the total. Flag any cell you cannot read.
Check your result. The rows say open 2 and closed 3. The total is 5.
